Adjacency in binary slicing tree is structural, not geometric: the inner-loop NM cannot fix topological adjacency failures. Two paths exist: (1) tree-sibling adjacency — a node is adjacent to its sibling in the tree; (2) cross-zone geometric adjacency — leaves from different subtrees that happen to share a boundary. Staircase/adjacency fails require a topology mutation that changes which nodes are siblings or which zones touch. This was proved empirically on programme-house: staircase fail from rot=0 layout could not be fixed by NM but was fixed by level_retype creating a two-C topology (2026-06-14/15).

collapse_global (94g) and any label/usage optimisation CANNOT fix geometry-intrinsic fails. The harbor-house 15-fail best layout contains long-thin cells that are useless whatever room usage is assigned — their width/proportion/crinkliness fails are shape-bound, not label slack. Two consequences: (1) do not over-claim collapse gains — only ~2-3 of that layout's fails are reclaimable relabel slack, the rest are geometry- or building-level bound; (2) the threshold objective must not be tuned to 'pass' a degenerate cell via a permissive room type — a metric-pass on a physically useless space is gaming, not a fix. Real remedies for these are geometry/topology search (cell shape) and circulation placement, filed separately, not the collapse.

collapse_global's Jacobi adjacency relaxation (homemaker-py-94g) is a synchronous per-round linear-assignment re-solve, which can 2-cycle indefinitely between two labellings that each satisfy ZERO adjacency requirements even though a permutation satisfying ALL of them exists -- proven on a minimal 4-cell chain (p1-q1-p2-q2, two disjoint adjacency pairs p1<->p2/q1<->q2) in test_two_opt_polish_escapes_jacobi_plateau. homemaker-py-9wi added Fitness._two_opt_adjacency_polish: a same-level pairwise-swap local search run after the Jacobi fixpoint, gated behind collapse_global(local_search=True) (default off, exposed as homemaker-collapse --local-search). Monotone by construction (a swap is kept only if it strictly increases total reward). Empirically on the 11 harbor-house evolved-*.dom/3m.dom/materialised-3M.dom layouts: 10 matched Jacobi-only exactly, 0 regressed, and evolved-anneal-3M.dom improved 21->19 fails (fixed a genuine mutual da1<->k1 adjacency miss the Jacobi loop couldn't reach).

An exact CP-SAT solve of collapse_global's relabelling (§39.273) is optimal-or-equal to the shipped Jacobi+2-opt on 40/60 designs and within 1-3 elsewhere, and its labelling scores better on 13 and worse on 13 at 100-2000x the cost: the collapse's objective (no daylight/access/connectivity) is the limit, not its solver.

Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (§39.204): cost exists to prevent WASTEFUL spending; a room smaller than the brief asks is not a saving. Cost must never trade against shortfall (rules out value/cost, value-cost, P/cost). If cost/waste is charged, charge area beyond the brief (e.g. surplus circulation), not total cost. A fixed-cost engine that pares rooms is a separate, unbuilt engine. cProfile on Python 3.14 makes a 28 ms score cost ~975 ms; the tax is per call, so it inflates small hot functions (Node.leaves, dict gets, Graph.copy) and its percentages are call counts, not time. Two 'costs' it named at 6% and 8% saved nothing when removed (DESIGN.md §39.136 second addendum, 2026-10-12). Before optimising a line it names: stub that line and time the whole score unprofiled (time.process_time, fastest of ~25), or wrap a few coarse functions with timers.

Deceptive valleys in topology search: when every single-step mutation from a target state passes through a high-fail intermediary (e.g. level_fix displaces a room into 5+ new fails), a compound operator that atomically applies two coordinated changes can escape. Design compound operators to land on the low-fail state directly, bypassing the deceptive gradient. Programme-house example: level_compound_fix atomically moves the level-constrained room AND re-inserts the displaced room adjacent to C in one step (operators.py, 2026-06-14).

Long jobs in this repo must outlive the session: start them with 'setsid nohup <script> > ~/homemaker-<name>.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &' (see experiments/run_ab_queue.sh, run_ab_queue2.sh, ../hm-moves/experiments/run_recordings.sh). A session background task dies with the session and, if it is a chain, killing one link starts the next. Stop processes by PID only -- 'pkill -f pattern' and 'pgrep -f pattern | kill' match your own shell and killed it three times on 2026-10-07. To stop a CHAIN of evolve phases, SIGKILL its bash loops first, then the searches: SIGTERM makes homemaker-evolve write its best and exit 0, so the loop would start the next phase (2026-10-22, run2.sh). A 'start B after A' must itself be a detached watcher (setsid nohup bash -c 'until grep -q ^done A.log; do sleep 300; done; exec B.sh'). Never rm a /tmp glob a just-started job may be using. On the owner's desktop a sweep uses all 8 threads, so container work beside it must be niced (10 is workable; at 19 a 100k run took 9.5 hours) and timed with time.process_time().

Staircase across storeys: a stair is a column of cells typed exactly 'E' at the SAME tree path on each storey it serves (owner rulings §39.72, §39.125; graph.stair_shaft, graph.stack_corners_in_use walks dom._above_node). It must reach the storey above and may stop below the top; a stacked 'C' is a corridor. An operator that divides/retypes a shaft cell on one storey breaks it unless it changes every storey in step: guard with operators._shaft_paths/_shaft_cells; mutate_repair_shaft (default on) cuts a new shaft. No intact shaft costs x0.0225.

A background waiter 'until ! pgrep -f PATTERN; do sleep; done' never exits: its own bash command line contains PATTERN, so pgrep always finds it (2026-11-07, Phase 1 tune). Wait on the job's LOG instead: until [ $(grep -c '^\[' log) -ge N ] || grep -q Traceback log; do sleep 30; done.

Proportion-aware constructive seeding (leu.2/§12.2): sizing seed cuts from target AREAS only regresses (thin slivers wreck aspect); you must ALSO pick each cut's rotation for child squareness. It is a convergence ACCELERATOR via a deeper local optimum around the constructed topology: wins where that topology is roughly right and budget is scarce (harbor -13%, maple -10% at 20k evals) but DELAYS small programmes where the seed must be restructured by undivide (programme-house regresses at fixed budget, yet reaches the floor given budget - speed, not asymptote). Default-on. Also: n_storeys must honour storey_minimum, not just level: keys (programme-house storey_minimum:2, all rooms level:0 - was seeded 1 storey short; cq1).

A filter that drops candidates must be shown sound before it is trusted, by running WITH and WITHOUT it and diffing what passes (seed_from_catalogue.py --check-prune is the worked example). Two plausible prunes were lossy in §39.148 (capacity prune lost outlines on health-centre; ladder prune lost 43-157 passing trees), and in §39.149 a shape-curve grid inversion that rounded INWARD falsely called 11 bins infeasible -- an 'infeasible' verdict is only sound if every approximation rounds outward (shapecurve hulls over-state feasibility, which is the safe direction).

After merging branches locally with --no-ff merges, plain 'git pull --rebase' tries to replay the branches' own commits and re-hits the DESIGN.md/DESIGN-INDEX append conflict (2026-10-24). pyproject.toml sets pytest pythonpath=["src"], so pytest ALWAYS imports the checkout's own src/ -- PYTHONPATH=<other>/src does nothing to a pytest run (it does for plain python scripts). A negative control 'run the new test against the old code' must swap the old file into the checkout (git show HEAD:path > path, run, restore), not point PYTHONPATH elsewhere; otherwise the control silently runs the new code and passes. Run-to-run reproducibility in homemaker-layout: serial search (workers=1) is byte-for-byte deterministic; parallel (workers>1) is now deterministic too AFTER fixing driver._run_batch to admit futures in submission order (was as_completed/completion order, bug xcy). Reproducibility holds only for a FIXED worker count — serial vs parallel differ because children-per-iteration is 1 vs n_workers (different batch granularity), which is expected, not a bug. The constructive seeder was NEVER nondeterministic: _assign_adjacency_aware has unique idx tiebreaks; comparing topologies with Python builtin hash() of the signature STRING is invalid (PYTHONHASHSEED salts str hashing per process) — use a stable hash (sha1) or genome.signature equality.

Sizing by arithmetic (DESIGN §39.109/§39.110, 2026-10-07): solver.solve_ratios recovers 77% of the fail gap on a COLD topology (closed-form area ratio 35%, Nelder-Mead 80 evals 7%) but makes a CHILD that inherits its parent's ratios worse by ~6 fails (86 of 96): evolved ratios encode daylight/access, which the solver's area/width/proportion model erases. Never re-size a child; only seeds/restarts are cold. solve_ratios needs max_nfev capped (~100): uncapped, one call ran >20 min. And the inner loop does little for a child: 20 evaluations keep 7 of the 11 wins 80 find (wins are nested); child_budget=80 has never been swept -- experiments/flag_ab.py child20/child40 is the box A/B. Experiment hygiene from the same night: seed per-artefact RNG from a HASH of the full path (low bytes of 'coldstart-...' are identical for every artefact; Python hash() is salted).

Unfold strategy for shared leaves (homemaker-py-8iv, resolved 2026-07-16): use the BALANCED GRID (operators._grow_balanced/_size_subtree_equal), NOT circulation-aware slicing. Slicing a shared leaf perpendicular to its access edge so every child touches the corridor was implemented + A/B-tested and LOST decisively (150k-eval warm-start polish from evolved-3M: slice 41 fails/3.5e-14 vs grid 25 fails/2.4e-09, grid ahead at every milestone). Reason: k rooms all touching one wall are intrinsically thin slices; that geometric debt (proportion/long/width) is unfixable without topology change, while the grid's squarer children let local search re-route access cheaply via level_retype/place_missing/level_fix. Lesson: at the sharing->no-sharing transition, prioritise squarer children and leave access to local search; do not reintroduce slicing in Schedule B (kpu).

A room's usage: is a bundle of access behaviours, so giving a room ONE new behaviour by relabelling it drags the rest along: calling the workshop 'utility' to let it be reached through another room also made it a dead end and cut two committed designs' ground floors in two. It got its own value 'workshop' (= living + the one difference). General method that caught it: price any objective change on every committed design before and after (experiments/diag_8b2u_score_cost.py --snapshot x2, then compare fail lists), and look hardest at designs that GAIN a fail (2026-10-12, DESIGN.md §39.138).

Never wait on 'pgrep -f <pattern>' from a loop whose own command line contains the pattern: it finds itself forever (2026-10-15, box idle overnight, §39.145). warm_x0 initialization bug pattern (fixed 2026-06-14): when a topology operator explicitly sets division ratios on a newly-created node (e.g. level_compound_fix sets node.division for t3), parent.ratios has no entry for that node (it was a leaf); defaulting it to 0.5 corrupts the inner loop's start and makes the operator invisible to lex comparison. Rule: only propagate a child ratio where the parent node was already divided, and stale hidden nodes revealed by structural mutations (swap flipping b.below) must not contribute pre-writeback values. Now lives in innerloop.warm_x0, called from driver.py.
